qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Must-attend B2B exhibitions (World of Concrete, Arab Health) and high-impact academic journal subscriptions (Taylor & Francis) demonstrate steady 3-5% annual pricing power above inflation; tangible ROIC >15%.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet). Informa's aggressive serial M&A rollup strategy (UBM, Ascential) has loaded the balance sheet with £2.7B+ in long-term debt and £10.4B in goodwill/intangibles, depressing FY25 interest coverage to an unsafe 0.6x (EBIT £94.6M vs interest £158.9M) and failing the peace-of-mind solvency standard.
qualitative.evidence: While Informa owns premier event franchises and Taylor & Francis journals, multi-year GAAP ROIC has been depressed to a 4.3% median by serial M&A. In FY25, reported net income plummeted to £11M and EBIT dropped to £94.6M against £158.9M in interest expense (0.6x coverage). Long-term debt of £2,727.6M exceeds 4x normalized net income, failing Gate 6 balance sheet criteria.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
